# Lists Core

Lists core business logic:

## Publishing a New Version

Publish new versions on master

Publishing a new version will require 4 parts

- Knowing your current version
- Knowing what kind of change your version is considered to be
- pushing the new tagged version
- passing CI

Run `git fetch --all` to ensure you have the most current versions locally.

Run `git describe --tags` to inspect the most current version of your repo. (You'll need this result
for later)

As an example, let's say the output of the current version of our published repo is
`@joltup/lists-core@1.0.1`.

Note: To decide what version you should update the repo to, follow semantic versioning as described
here https://www.jvandemo.com/a-simple-guide-to-semantic-versioning/

Continuing in our example, and knowing that our current version is `@joltup/lists-core@1.0.1`
from running the previously listed bash command. Let's say for example that we made a backwards
compatible bug fix, and we only want to make a minor patch version change. We know we'll want to
update from `1.0.1` to `1.0.2`.

Therefore we will run `git tag @joltup/lists-core@1.0.2` (notice the update version now). Which
sets the current repo to have a new version.

Then I would push the update tag version up with git using `git push origin @joltup/lists-core@1.0.2` (notice again the new version #)

At this point your new version will be passing through the CI server and if it passes, you'll have
published a new version.
